articles.title: Peter Medak obituary
articles.summary: Film and television director who won plaudits for The Ruling Class, The Changeling and The Krays. In 2013, when Martin Scorsese compiled a brief list of his favourite horror films, he placed the eerie and overlooked 1980 ghost story The Changeling in the company of classics such as The Shining, The…
body: The Changeling concerns a composer ( George C Scott ) who is grieving the deaths of his wife and daughter in a road accident. After moving into a long-vacant Seattle mansion where things start going bump in the night, he becomes convinced that a spectral presence is trying to communicate with him.

A generation raised on slasher films might now be underwhelmed by the low-key frights, which include a bath that runs itself, a cobwebbed wheelchair and visions of a child’s face warped underwater. But with its subtlety and patience, and the prioritising of atmosphere over revelation, the movie remains chilling today.

It represented a rare foray into horror for Medak, who was already admired for The Ruling Class (1972), a madcap satire starring an Oscar-nominated Peter O’Toole as an aristocrat who believes himself to be Jesus Christ. The critic Janet Maslin identified in the director a “droll affinity for eccentric behaviour”.

articles.title: ‘Cher Adores Michael Douglas,’ Icon’s Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for ‘Moonstruck’
articles.summary: Cher is responding with grace to Michael Douglas’ viral diss over her 1988 Oscar win for “Moonstruck.” A representative for the music and acting icon told Entertainment Weekly point blank: “Cher adores Michael Douglas.” At the 60th Academy Awards in April 1988, Cher took home the prize for best…
body: “Michael, be kind,” Close then responded while turning to Douglas as the studio audience laughed.

All three actors attended the 1988 Oscars as nominees, with Cher winning best actress for “Moonstruck” and Douglas winning best actor for his role in Oliver Stone’s “Wall Street.” Douglas was the sole nominee for his movie, while “Moonstruck” was up for six awards, including best picture. The romantic comedy also won Oscars for adapted screenplay and supporting actress (Olympia Dukakis). “Fatal Attraction,” meanwhile, was also nominated for six Oscars but went home empty handed. Both movies battled for best picture and best director but lost to “The Last Emperor” and Bernardo Bertolucci, respectively.

articles.title: Oscar Predictions: Animated Feature — A New and Competitive Era for the Medium That Isn’t Just for Kids
articles.summary: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis.
body: Best Animated Feature Predictions Commentary (Updated: Nov. 3, 2026): This year, animated features aren’t just for kids. And that’s a good thing.

Laika’s “Wildwood” is the company’s first PG-13 film in its 17 years as a feature studio. At 130 minutes, it ties the record for the longest English-language animated film ever made. Director and producer Travis Knight is already an Oscar nominee for “Kubo and the Two Strings” and has earned considerable respect from his peers and audiences alike. “Wildwood” is among the year’s most acclaimed films and, despite a less-than-stellar box office performance, currently looks like the one to beat.

Knight was among the filmmakers featured in this year’s Pixels and Pencils panel, Variety’s conversation with animation directors at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival. He was joined by Brad Bird (“ Ray Gunn ”), Daniel Chong (“Hoppers”), Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado (“Forgotten Island”) and Leah Nelson (“Tangles”), all of whom are also in the animated feature race.

articles.title: China’s first AI-generated film is a flop. Some still see it as the future of cinema
articles.summary: Chinese investors placing high value on AI despite unpopularity of Sanxingdui: Future Past. China’s first fully AI-generated movie has flopped, earning just 1.7m yuan (£191,000) at the box office despite costing “tens of millions” to make, according to its producer. But is it any good?
body: But is it any good? The Guardian watched Sanxingdui: Future Past in a virtually empty cinema in Beijing, and found it no worse than plenty of human-centred mindless action flicks.

Sanxingdui tells a confusing tale of a future society in which every decision has been outsourced to algorithms and AI, leading to a global catastrophe. The only way to avert the impending doom is to unlock the hidden code that is hidden in the Sanxingdui, bronze sculptures linked to the ancient kingdom of Shu. Cue astronauts racing through ancient Egypt and archeologists diving through space-time vortices.
All of the film’s visuals and some of its sound effects were created using AI, while it was edited by humans.

articles.title: ‘The Elder Scrolls 6’ Title Revealed (Gaming News Roundup)
articles.summary: Bethesda Game Studios has officially revealed the subtitle and logo for “The Elder Scrolls 6.” The sixth edition was announced as “Sentinel” alongside a logo reveal in a video message from longtime franchise director Todd Howard as part of Bethesda’s 40th anniversary Tuesday.
body: Sentinel is a city within the Hammerfell province on Tamriel, the continent where “The Elder Scrolls” is set. Hammerfell is west of Cyrodiil, where the fourth installment “Oblivion” (2006) took place, and southwest of “Skyrim,” which is still the studio’s most played game.

“The Elder Scrolls 6” was first announced in 2018 during Bethesda’s E3 2018 conference and entered active production in 2023 after the launch of “Starfield.” Howard said in 2021 that he anticipated the game could be released 15-17 years after “Skyrim,” potentially putting fans still a few years away from playing “Sentinel.”
As the release of “Grand Theft Auto VI” looms closer, digital pre-loading is set to begin on Nov. 10.

Players can pre-load the game on PlayStation 5 at midnight local time in respective time zones and on XBOX Series X and S at midnight GMT. The pre-load file will require up to 212 GB depending on the device, and code-in-box versions for both consoles is set to be available from retailers starting Nov. 12. Details on how to pre-load “GTA 6” are available on the Rockstar Support website.

articles.title: Netflix Orders YA Drama ‘Prep’ Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Novel From Nicole Taylor
articles.summary: Netflix has given a straight-to-series order to the drama “Prep,” based on the novel of the same name by Curtis Sittenfeld. The show is officially described as a coming-of-age story about “scholarship girl Lee Fiora’s high school years at Ault, a prestigious New England boarding school, and her…
body: Nicole Taylor will adapt the book for the screen and will serve as showrunner and executive producer. Will Ferrell, Jessica Elbaum, and Alix Taylor will executive produce for Gloria Sanchez Productions. Sittenfeld is also an executive producer.

“’Prep’ is my all time favourite novel and I have longed to adapt it for the entire twenty years since I first read it and found myself reflected uncannily back,” Taylor said. “There is no more acute depiction of the introspective, bookish self-conscious adolescent girl and no more truthful or excoriating take on the perils of social mobility than in Curtis Sittenfeld’s beautiful first novel. I am overjoyed to be adapting for Netflix.”

Taylor most recently created the popular series “One Day” starring Leo Woodall and Ambika Mod, which aired on Netflix in 2024. Her other credits include the feature “The Wild Rose” and shows like “Three Girls,” “Dracula,” and “The White Queen.”

articles.title: Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant review – slime and silliness in amusing New Zealand comedy horror
articles.summary: Mucus, alien gristle, a tentacle-bearing penis and, of course, the pregnancy of the title are all borne with deadpan calmness in this underplayed comedy. In this amusingly silly exercise in gross-out body horror and bathos from New Zealand, thirtysomething underachiever Mary (Hannah Lynch) finds…
body: Fortunately, the cast is well up for serving this sort of underplayed comedy, especially supporting players Yvette Parsons and Jackie van Beek, as Mary and Arlo’s single mums Cynthia and Ann respectively. For example, somewhere towards the end (and don’t worry, there’s nothing to spoil here), Cynthia gets a little het up about Mary farting too much, after a nest of mucus, tissue and alien gristle shoots out of Mary’s nether regions. Ann, on the other hand, gets quite concerned about the mess all this is making of her immaculate flat, and keeps apologising for the disorder to anyone who shows up, including unflappable paramedics Sofia (Karen O’Leary) and Sophie (Ariadne Baltazar).

Is it all meant to be a parable about the anxieties of single motherhood and the changes pregnancy wreaks on the female body? Yes, sure, if you want. But subtext is less the point than slow burns and slime, and that honest directness make the end result rather winning.

articles.title: Andrew Scott drama Elsinore leads British independent film award nominations
articles.summary: Elsinore is in contention for 12 Bifas, including for Scott’s highly praised performance, while Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, Ashley Walters’ Animol and Mike Leigh’s Tender Loving Care are also recognised.
body: Elsinore, the drama in which Andrew Scott plays the actor Ian Charleson as he takes on Shakespeare’s Hamlet in the last months of his life, before he died of Aids in 1990, has emerged as the leading contender for the British independent film awards (Bifas).

The film, which is directed by Simon Stone and co-stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper and Johnny Flynn, received 12 nominations, including best British independent film, best director for Stone and best lead performance for Scott. Elsinore has collected rave reviews since its premiere at the Telluride film festival in September, with the Guardian’s Benjamin Lee describing it as “a devastating movie [that] is a reminder of Charleson’s strength and the many men like him and it implores us to remember them too”. Scott is also already being tipped as the favourite for the best actor Oscar – and he would be the first out gay actor to win.

articles.title: BBC Wales cuts risk 'irreversible deterioration', warns first minister
articles.summary: He says the corporation could breach its public service obligations if it proceeds as planned.
body: The first minister has warned of an "irreversible deterioration" in the way the BBC covers Wales, if the corporation proceeds with cuts as planned.
The warning comes in a letter to BBC director-general Matt Brittin, which has been seen by BBC Wales.
The letter also claims that the changes could lead to the BBC being in breach of its public service obligations under its Royal Charter.
In reply, Brittin told First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth that the BBC takes its obligations to Wales "extremely seriously".

articles.title: Celebrity loses injunction bid but will stay anonymous pending appeal
articles.summary: The unnamed man asked for an injunction to stop his identity being reported in connection with allegations against him.
body: A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the court saying the man's claim for an injunction was denied.

But the judge said a temporary injunction preventing the man from being named and the allegations published should remain in place, in order to allow the celebrity to appeal against the judgment, with anonymity and reporting restrictions remaining in force during the period allowed for any appeal.

ITN and the Guardian have said they believe it is in the public interest to publish allegations that the man abused his status to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".
The man, who denies the allegations, said any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself, and that the court should prevent any publication or broadcast.

articles.title: Rebecca Gayheart Opens Up About Eric Dane’s Final Days: “Everything Shifted”
articles.summary: The wife of the 'Grey's Anatomy' star, who died in February, less than a year after announcing his ALS diagnosis, spoke about how she had "no idea that was it" when Dane made his last hospital trip.
body: Rebecca Gayheart is opening up about Eric Dane ‘s final days timed to the release of the Grey’s Anatomy star’s posthumous memoir, My Book of Day s.
Dane died in February, less than a year after announcing his ALS diagnosis.

The actress, who married Dane in 2004 before embarking upon a divorce in 2018 and having that dismissed in 2025, said it didn’t initially dawn on her that the Euphoria actor’s last trip to the hospital would mark the beginning of the end.

“I said, ‘Listen, I’ll be back. I have a dinner. I’m going to this event.’ I had no idea that that was it, that that week was going to be our last week,” Gayheart said. “And nor did my daughters. It really took a few days for us to understand the gravity of what that last trip to the hospital meant.”
